spec.model: none; isolated original BF16 inputs with positive power-of-two BF16 exponent encoding
spec.purpose: Isolated matrix recovery of original K16 paired exponent maxima. Encode each supported nonzero BF16 exponent e as2^(5e), use one positive zero-C BF16 WMMA per group and recover the integer maximum from1.5 times its result. The explicit relative native-error condition is0.25, with exact native zero preservation; no universal hardware bound is claimed. Unsupported exponent rows and invalid recovery retain original scalar per-product maxima. Eight waves prepare all16 group maxima into LDS, then original scalar FP32 products and every canonical ordered K16 carry produce complete QK scores. Original scalar eligibility flags and four-byte query/key encodings belong to the candidate and are timed and independently checked. No model load or production dispatcher change. Core outputs compare to independent CPU paired exponents and double sums of positive powers; all score bits, immutable inputs and guards compare to original complete canonical GPU scores and CPU dots

compiled_kernel_resources.scope: Read-only ELF metadata from the SHA-bound Windows executable. Static register/shared/scratch declarations are not measured occupancy or a performance explanation.

implementation: Supported BF16 exponents e in[-12,12] encode as positive2^(5e); zero stays zero and other exponents get an invalid marker. Every positive K16 dot lies between one and sixteen times its leading power. Under explicit relative native-error<=0.25 and exact-zero preservation, the FP32 exponent of1.5 times the native dot, floor-divided by5, recovers the original paired maximum exactly. Eight waves recover all16 group maxima into shared memory before scalar score work. Scalar products, original modulo reduction and every ordered K16 carry are unchanged. Invalid encodings/recovery use original per-product maxima and original scalar-domain/carry rejection restarts the full canonical dot. Three64/128/256 windows share BF16 operands; candidates own all query/key encodings and scalar-domain flags.
correctness_scope: The host recovery band and ordered canonical groups are checked independently. Native generated matrices compare every recovered maximum to CPU exponent pairs, all operand encodings to independent CPU encoding and positive native dots to double sums of powers, including zero and invalid rows. The broad relative-error condition is still an assumption about the native instruction, not a universal hardware proof. All generated/captured QK score bits and unused score tails match original complete canonical GPU scores on every warmup and measured attempt, with independent CPU dot samples. Prepared query bytes and flags are checked after each variant/slab, key preparation and original operands at invocation end. Component extension repeats the first1023 original rows; no new GB10 token loop is created. Reference outputs never select or compute candidate work.
timing_scope: The native maximum fixture reports correctness only. Full QK includes matrix maximum recovery, scalar products and canonical carries. Every slab timer includes candidate query encoding and invalid-flag clearing; one key encoding/flag clear is added once. The selected control includes its own full Q/K preparation. Variants rotate across slabs, each with one warmup and three completed measurements. Allocation, reset and validation are outside component clocks; all bounded process walls and source/binary identities are attached. No probability, PV, model load, TTFT or token generation is measured.

decision.decision: Keep matrix-recovered maxima isolated. Every native maximum and generated/captured QK bit passes, but complete q8192 current/W64/W128/W256 medians are352.9428/653.2891/637.2444/646.938ms. The additional matrix/LDS work does not yield a faster complete QK route. Embedded compiler metadata reports130 VGPRs and zero private scratch for all four score kernels; this is static resource evidence, not measured occupancy or proof of the dominant cause. Investigate separating the extended scalar fallback from the selected prepared fast kernel, preserving original arithmetic and full output comparison.
